header.title: Free build
header.intro: The build is €0 for a typical business or brochure site, with a minimum term of 36 months on the hosting subscription. After that it is monthly cancellable. The plan does not follow the number of pages but how much the site stores and how much traffic it takes: pages cost nothing, a media library and a database do. Every plan states exactly where the limit sits before an upgrade is needed.

header.title: Two routes
header.intro: Free build. €0 for a typical business or brochure site. 36 months minimum, then monthly cancellable.

layout.text: Or pay for the build: from €2,500, then ongoing and cancellable monthly with one month’s notice. A paid build can, by arrangement, be spread over the first year. All prices exclude 21% VAT. A paid build scales with complexity.

header.title: Four plans
header.intro: This is the subscription the end client takes with Rinsly: including when a partner designed the site. The client always owns the site and the data. We invoice in advance, monthly or yearly; paying yearly gets you a month free, two on Growth. All prices exclude 21% VAT. This is what you pay Rinsly; if a design studio invoices you themselves, their price applies.

layout.text: Over a limit? We tell you, and you choose: pay per unit (€1 per extra GB of media, €5 per extra GB of database, €2 per extra million requests a month) or move up a plan. We never throttle your site quietly.

header.title: Your invoice, your price, your brand
header.intro: Reselling and your own branding are allowed. If you invoice the end client yourself, you buy from Rinsly at list minus your percentage, put design and hosting on one invoice, and set the price and your own tiers if you want. You may name Rinsly the way anyone names Cloudflare: hosting at Rinsly. The percentage is the same number on both invoice routes, from 0% to 35% of the recurring subscription revenue excluding VAT, per settled invoice.

cards.title: +10% Exclusivity
cards.description: New client work and updates go to Rinsly. Clients already hosted elsewhere stay where they are. A big update (rebuild, migration, redesign, substantial expansion) triggers a migration conversation.

cards.title: +5% Relationship management
cards.description: The partner is the first line. The client calls the partner; the partner files a ticket. Rinsly does no direct client contact.

cards.title: +5% Marketing
cards.description: The partner names and sells Rinsly as their hosting partner.

header.title: You design, we do the rest

layout.title: Three steps, and only one of them is yours
layout.caption: You deliver the design system. Rinsly builds it as a real application on the shared engine and takes it live, then runs edge hosting, SSL, uptime monitoring, daily backups (continuous point-in-time database restore via Cloudflare D1 Time Travel and a nightly media backup), security and CMS updates.

layout.title: What would you take home?
layout.intro: Pick a plan, drag the number of clients and tick what you would take on. The rate and your share follow along.
layout.footnote: Each volume level is +5% and the levels are cumulative, so the ladder tops out at 35% of the recurring subscription revenue excluding VAT, per settled invoice. One-off build fees and meerwerk are not shared. Commission accrues when the invoice is settled, not when it is issued, and is paid on that client’s billing interval. This is an indication, not an offer.

layout.title: Who sends which invoice
layout.caption: Setup A: Rinsly invoices the end client at list and pays the commission once that invoice is settled. Setup B: the partner invoices their own client and buys at list minus their ladder percentage. Either way the agreement runs between Rinsly and the end client.
